description: Start of the reference period. In components_of_growth_annual.csv each year runs from July 1 to June 30 and is stored as July 1 of its first year (1971-07-01 is 1971/1972, 2025-07-01 is 2025/2026). In the two quarterly files it is the first day of the quarter (2026-04-01 is April to June 2026).
components_of_growth_annual.csv only. Reference year exactly as published, for example 2025/2026, meaning July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

Geography as published: Canada, the ten provinces and the three territories. Before 1991/1992 (annual) or July 1991 (quarterly) only Northwest Territories including Nunavut is published, and Northwest Territories and Nunavut appear separately after that.
Statistics Canada Dissemination Geography Unique Identifier for the geography.

components_of_growth_annual.csv and international_migration_quarterly.csv only. Component as published: Immigrants, Emigrants, Returning emigrants, Net emigration, Net temporary emigration, Net non-permanent residents, Non-permanent residents, inflows, Non-permanent residents, outflows, and, in the annual file only, Births, Deaths, Net interprovincial migration and Residual deviation. Net emigration is emigrants less returning emigrants, plus net temporary emigration up to June 2016.
Unit of measure for value, as published: Persons in the two components files and Number in the natural increase file.
Statistics Canada numeric code for the unit of measure.
Scale of value as published. units in all three files, so a value of 1000 means 1,000 persons or events.
Statistics Canada numeric code for the scalar factor.
Statistics Canada vector identifier for the series. Useful if you want to pull the same series again.
Statistics Canada coordinate string that locates the series inside the official table.

The published count of persons or events in the period. Net components can be negative, for example net non-permanent residents when more people leave that group than join it. Empty when Statistics Canada did not publish a figure (status ..). Official values were not altered.
Statistics Canada status symbol. .. means not available for that reference period and value is empty. Empty status means a regular published value.
Additional Statistics Canada symbol when present. Empty in all three files in this snapshot.

t if Statistics Canada has terminated this series, otherwise empty. In this snapshot it is set only in natural_increase_quarterly.csv, for the marriage series and for the combined Northwest Territories including Nunavut births and deaths series that ended in 1991.
Number of decimal places Statistics Canada uses when displaying the value.
